findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy: none; pct: 100; rua: true

findings.deal_impact: DMARC is monitor-only, so the domain can be spoofed, increasing BEC and wire-fraud risk for the company, customers and deal counterparties; underwriters may require enforcement.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, validating all legitimate senders and alignment first.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier: ~all; lookup_count: 2

findings.deal_impact: SPF soft-fail weakens anti-spoofing controls and phishing resistance, contributing to email-fraud risk alongside monitor-only DMARC.

remediation.summary: Audit authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all once legitimate sources are confirmed.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled
findings.deal_impact: Without DNSSEC, DNS responses lack authenticated integrity, leaving a residual cache-poisoning/redirection weakness; low standalone deal impact.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at the registrar/DNS provider and verify the DS record and chain of trust.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems
findings.deal_impact: Four risky CT-logged names suggest possible admin, legacy or staging exposure that attackers can enumerate; requires validation of whether they are live and hardened before close.

remediation.summary: Inventory the four risky hostnames, decommission or restrict legacy/staging/admin services, and enforce MFA and patching on any retained.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 unique hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests attack-surface sprawl that may exceed asset inventory discipline; low direct impact if inventoried.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames against the CMDB/asset inventory, retire unknown assets, and add CT monitoring.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: The www host offers deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1, weakening transport security and potentially failing customer, PCI-adjacent or insurer baseline requirements.

remediation.summary: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 on www, retaining TLS 1.2+ with current cipher configuration.

findings.title: HSTS not set
findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS on both hosts leaves users exposed to downgrade/stripping attacks; a quick baseline hygiene gap with limited standalone deal impact.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security on apex and www after confirming HTTPS-only operation, then consider preload.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001; vendor: ExampleGate; product: ExampleGate SSL-VPN; match_tier: appliance_exposed; match_level: product; note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: a KEV-listed SSL-VPN appliance fingerprint was seen, but version/patch status is not verified. If vulnerable, this is a high-priority edge-compromise, insurability and closing-condition risk.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate SSL-VPN version/patch against CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, patch or isolate, and review appliance logs for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type: state_ag_breach_notice; date: 2025-08-14; Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months: 14; entity_match: exact

findings.deal_impact: A disclosed breach 14 months ago affecting ~3,100 individuals raises regulatory, litigation, customer-notification and cyber-insurance diligence risk; scope and remediation closure should be confirmed.

remediation.summary: Obtain breach investigation, regulator correspondence and remediation evidence; confirm notification completion and lessons-learned controls.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: Elevated account takeover and unauthorized production access risk for administrative/service-desk accounts due to missing MFA enforcement; remediation was still in progress at the report date with migration not expected until Q3 2026.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: Elevated post-termination unauthorized access risk, with retention up to 19 business days, while de-provisioning remains manual pending automation.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: Two-week period in November 2025 in which security alerts were not reviewed, creating a detection and incident-response blind spot for that period.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: Limited change-management deviation involving emergency hotfixes without documented pre-deployment approval, with procedure now requiring post-deployment approval within 48 hours.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: Infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (Infrastructure hosting; production workloads run in Nimbus Cloud Services) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, not same-day revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC7.2 exception: for Nov 10-23, 2025, alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none, so DMARC is monitoring-only and not enforced; the domain can be spoofed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system, with approx. 3,100 individuals notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT presence alone doesn't prove a host is live; however legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (2026-08-14) certs within the last 12 months show active maintenance, contradicting decommissioning a while back.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: Annual pen test control had no exceptions, but the test reported 2 high-severity findings, contradicting 'clean, no highs.' Remediation was out of scope.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 A1.2-01 was tested with no exceptions: production data is backed up daily to immutable storage and restore tests are performed quarterly, corroborating the claim.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: No bridge letter was provided after the period ended 2026-03-31; E-030 is only unaudited management stating a plan to obtain one upon request, not positive tested evidence it can be obtained.

deal_recommendations.text: Require verification of the ExampleGate SSL-VPN version and patch status, a compromise assessment of appliance logs, and a bring-down of security representations before signing, aligned to Days 0–30 [F-008].
Expand the review to independently assess the KEV-listed exposure and validate management representations against primary evidence, completing the initial scope in Days 0–30 [F-008].
Seek a specific indemnity for losses arising from the pre-closing disclosed incident, with breach investigation and remediation evidence to be delivered in Days 31–60 [F-009].
Expect the known disclosed incident to be excluded from representations and warranties coverage, and confirm that position during the Days 31–60 review of incident evidence [F-009].
Confirm cyber insurability before close, including underwriter requirements on DMARC enforcement and the MFA and de-provisioning remediation scheduled for Days 31–60 [F-001] [F-010] [F-011].

Covenant completion after close of the remaining access, monitoring, change-management, email-authentication, hostname, transport-security, breach and bridge-letter remediation across Days 31–60 and Days 61–100 [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009] [F-014].

No price adjustment is warranted, as total remediation of $142K–$643K, phased from Days 0–30 through After day 100, is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band [F-001] [F-002] [F-003] [F-004] [F-005] [F-006] [F-007] [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012] [F-013] [F-014] [F-015].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. Rated D at 56.8, capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure, a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months, and multiple management statements contradicted by evidence [F-008] [F-009] [C-001] [C-005]. Key risks: A KEV-listed SSL-VPN appliance is internet-facing with version and patch status unverified. A disclosed breach 14 months ago affected ~3,100 individuals. MFA and timely de-provisioning exceptions leave admin and post-termination access exposed, and monitor-only DMARC allows domain spoofing [F-008] [F-009] [F-010] [F-011] [F-001]. Management credibility: Of 9 claims assessed, 7 were contradicted, 1 unsupported, 1 supported. Management credibility is materially weakened because core statements on MFA, offboarding, monitoring, DMARC, and incident history are contradicted by evidence [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005] [C-006] [C-007]. Next steps: Immediately verify the SSL-VPN version and compromise status in Days 0–30, obtain breach and SOC 2 bridge evidence, independently validate management representations, and confirm insurability before signing [F-008] [F-009] [F-014] [F-001].
